Build a premium website with Jarvis

Follow the steps in order. The file is here as a download button, and every message has a Copy button. Once you send the first website message, Jarvis guides you too, so you’re never on your own.

About 2 hours in total, mostly Jarvis workingTick each step as you go; your progress is savedDon’t unzip the files

Before you start

What you need, about 5 minutes to check

Step 15 min

Have these ready

Building a client website takes about one to two hours of Jarvis working, with a few short moments where you need to click or answer. Do it on a computer.

  1. A computer with Chrome or Safari, not a phone.
  2. Jarvis 2.0 already installed (from the Jarvis 2.0 setup guide).
  3. Jarvis set to Claude Opus 5.5 for the build: open Jarvis, Agent Settings, and choose Claude Opus 5.5 as the model. It uses more credits but builds a much better site. You can switch back after launch.
  4. Only for some websites: a card to add about 10 US dollars to Higgsfield, which makes AI photos and videos. Jarvis tells you at the plan step if your site needs it; most don’t.
  5. Your client’s details: business name, what they do, their area, phone, email, address, opening hours, services and prices, and any logo or photos they have.
You’ll seeEverything above is ready, and Jarvis is open in one tab.
If it looks differentDon’t have all the client details? Start anyway. Jarvis marks anything missing in [brackets] so you can fill it in later.

Add the website skills

One file, about 2 minutes

Step 21 min

Download the website skills

This file gives Jarvis everything it needs to research, design and build websites.

  1. Click the button above to download the file.
  2. Don’t open or unzip it. Jarvis needs it exactly as it is.
You’ll seeA file called jarvis-skills-module-7-delivery.zip in your Downloads folder.
If it looks differentNothing downloaded? Open this guide in Chrome or Safari instead of a preview window.
Step 31 min

Install them in Jarvis

Jarvis adds the skills and tells you when it is ready.

  1. Open your Jarvis chat.
  2. Click + and attach the file you just downloaded.
  3. Copy the message below, paste it in the same message, and send.
Send to Jarvis, with the file attached
Install Module 7, Fulfilment, from the attached file. Add every skill inside, replace any older versions, and don't run anything yet. When you're done, show me what you installed and where we start.
You’ll seeJarvis lists 4 skills: scoping agent, website research, brand guide and premium website.
If it looks differentIf Jarvis says something else must come first, follow its steps, then send the message again.

Set up Higgsfield (only if Jarvis asks)

Most websites don’t need it. Skip this stage unless Jarvis says your site needs photos or videos

Step 43 min

Create your Higgsfield account

Only do this stage if Jarvis said your website needs photos or videos (for example a garden company, a restaurant or a real estate site). Higgsfield makes them; Jarvis uses it for you, but it needs its own account with a little money on it.

  1. Go to console.higgsfield.ai and sign up (or sign in if you already use Higgsfield).
  2. Important: this is the API console. A normal Higgsfield subscription does not cover it, so you add a balance here even if you already pay for Higgsfield.
You’ll seeYou are signed in to the Higgsfield console.
If it looks differentThe page looks different from these steps? Menu names change from time to time. Look for the closest match.
Step 52 min

Add a balance

Each image and video costs a little. Jarvis always tells you the cost and waits for your OK before spending anything.

  1. In the console, find Billing, Credits or Balance.
  2. Add about 10 US dollars. That covers a typical website.
You’ll seeYour balance shows in the console.
If it looks differentCard declined? Try another card, or contact Higgsfield’s support.
Step 62 min

Create an API key

The key is how Jarvis logs in to Higgsfield for you. It comes in two parts.

  1. In the console, find API Keys and click Create.
  2. You get two values: a Key ID and a Key Secret.
  3. Copy both into a safe note for a minute. The Secret is shown only once. If you lose it, just create a new key.
  4. Never paste these keys into the Jarvis chat. You will put them into a secure box in the next step.
You’ll seeYou have the Key ID and the Key Secret copied.
If it looks differentClosed the page before copying the Secret? Delete that key and create a new one.
Step 72 min

Save the key in Jarvis, safely

Jarvis opens a secure box for keys. What you type there is saved privately and never shows in the chat.

  1. Send Jarvis the message below.
  2. A box called Set secrets appears with two fields.
  3. Paste the Key ID into HIGGSFIELD_KEY_ID and the Key Secret into HIGGSFIELD_KEY_SECRET.
  4. If Higgsfield shows you one combined key instead of two parts, paste the whole key into HIGGSFIELD_KEY_ID.
  5. Click Submit Secrets (not Skip).
Send to Jarvis
I want to connect Higgsfield. Open the secure secret card so I can save my key ID as HIGGSFIELD_KEY_ID and my key secret as HIGGSFIELD_KEY_SECRET.
You’ll seeJarvis confirms both keys are saved, makes one small test image, and asks once how much it may spend per website without asking (it suggests 15 US dollars). After that it never asks about cost unless a site would go over.
If it looks differentJarvis says the key was not accepted? Create a new key in the console and save it again.

Build the website

Jarvis does the work, you answer and approve

Step 81 min

Start the website

One message starts everything. From here Jarvis guides you.

  1. Send the message below.
Send to Jarvis
Use the premium website skill to build a website for my client. Ask me what you need first.
You’ll seeJarvis asks you up to 8 questions in one message. Building in Claude Opus 5.5 gives the best result.
If it looks differentBuilding a site for your own agency? Write "for my own agency" instead of "for my client".
Step 95 min

Answer the questions

The better your answers, the better the website. Answer everything in one reply.

  1. The client: business name, what they do, city and area.
  2. The style: sleek and modern, classic and elegant, warm and natural, bold and energetic, or "you decide".
  3. How much movement: Clean (calm, one or two meaningful moments, best for most businesses) or Expressive (animation-rich). Not sure? Choose Clean.
  4. Contact details for the website, and the email address where new enquiries should go.
  5. Services, and prices if they show prices.
  6. What they already have: logo, colours, photos, team photos, recent work, real reviews, and their Instagram or Google profile. Real photos make the site feel premium.
  7. The one thing the website should make people do (call, book, ask for a quote), and any websites they like.
  8. The language of the website, and formal or informal if that matters.
You’ll seeJarvis researches the market for a few minutes, then shows you what it found.
If it looks differentNot sure about something? Write "not sure". Jarvis handles it.
Step 105 min

Pick a brand

Jarvis designs three looks for the business, each with a logo, colours and fonts. This decides how the whole site looks.

  1. Read the three options. Jarvis may also give you a link to see them side by side.
  2. Reply with your choice, for example: "Option 2".
  3. You can mix them, for example: "Option 2, with the colours from option 1".
You’ll seeJarvis confirms the brand and moves on to the plan.
If it looks differentDon’t like any of them? Tell Jarvis what you want instead, in plain words.
Step 115 min

Approve the plan

Jarvis shows you the full plan: every section, the animations, and the media level: built in code (most sites, free), a few AI photos, or cinematic videos. If your site needs photos or videos, do the Higgsfield stage above first.

  1. Read the plan. The cost is shown for information; within your budget Jarvis won’t ask about it again.
  2. Ask for changes if you want any, or reply "Yes, build it".
You’ll seeJarvis starts making the images and videos and building the site.
If it looks differentCost too high? Ask for the Premium version (photos only, no videos). It is cheaper and faster.
Step 1210 min

Help Jarvis create the website app

Jarvis needs a new app in Base44 to hold the website. It gives you the exact words to send, and the Base44 builder does the rest.

  1. When Jarvis asks, copy its message into the Base44 build box (where you build new apps) and send it.
  2. Base44 may show cards that say Approve, for example installing packages or adding screens. That is normal: click Approve on each one.
  3. If the builder stops halfway and asks to continue, type continue.
  4. If a box asks for secrets you don’t have, click Skip.
  5. Tell Jarvis when the builder has finished.
You’ll seeJarvis keeps building and tells you when the site is ready to review.
If it looks differentUnsure what Base44 is asking? Take a screenshot and send it to Jarvis.
Step 1330 to 90 min

Wait while Jarvis works

Making videos takes time, and Jarvis checks the website on phone, tablet and desktop before showing you.

  1. You can leave Jarvis working and come back.
  2. If Higgsfield needs more money, Jarvis tells you exactly what to do. Add credit in the console, then say continue.
You’ll seeJarvis sends you a review link.
If it looks differentNothing has happened for a long time? Ask Jarvis "Where are we with the website?"

Review and launch

Check it, fix it, go live

Step 1410 min

Review on your phone first

Most of your client’s customers will see the site on a phone, so check that first.

  1. Open the review link on your phone. Scroll the whole page.
  2. Then check it on your computer.
  3. Send Jarvis every change in one message, in plain words. For example: "Make the phone number bigger" or "Change the second photo".
You’ll seeJarvis makes the changes and tells you when they are done.
If it looks differentSomething looks broken? Send Jarvis a screenshot.
Step 153 min

Test the form

Every enquiry should reach your client by email. Test it before launch.

  1. On the website, fill in the form with your own details and send it.
  2. Check that the enquiry email arrived where you asked, and that you got a confirmation email. Check the spam folder too.
You’ll seeBoth emails arrived.
If it looks differentNo email? Tell Jarvis: "The form email didn’t arrive." It checks and fixes it.
Step 165 min

Fill in the missing details

Anything in [brackets] is a fact Jarvis did not have, like a licence number or opening hours. These must be filled in before launch.

  1. Ask Jarvis: "Show me everything still in brackets."
  2. Send the real details, or ask Jarvis to remove anything the client does not have.
You’ll seeNo [brackets] left on the website.
If it looks differentNever guess these. Ask your client.
Step 1715 min

Launch

Jarvis checks everything one last time, then helps you publish, connect your client’s own web address, and hand over.

  1. Send the message below and follow Jarvis’s steps.
  2. The web address (domain) must belong to your client, in their own account.
Send to Jarvis
Let's launch. Run the final checks, then walk me through publishing, connecting my client's domain, and the handover.
You’ll seeThe website is live on your client’s web address, and Jarvis gives you a handover page for your client.
If it looks differentYour client doesn’t have a web address yet? Jarvis explains how they can buy one.
Stuck anywhere? Send Jarvis a screenshot. It knows each step.
